skills.name: Establish compatible fraction form
skills.definition: Prepare operands so fraction parts are subtraction-ready by creating a common denominator and/or converting fractions to equivalent forms with matching denominators.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept as a single skill because finding a common denominator is a distinct preparation operation with its own common error patterns and is diagnostically separable from mixed-number normalization and from subtraction itself.

skills.name: Normalize mixed/whole-number operands
skills.definition: Rewrite whole numbers or mixed numbers into a subtraction-ready structure, such as adding a zero-fraction part, normalizing a nonstandard mixed number, or separating whole and fractional parts for later computation.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept as a single skill because operand normalization is a preparation skill, but it is meaningfully different from common-denominator work: students may know how to align denominators yet still fail to rewrite whole or mixed numbers appropriately.

skills.name: Subtract and regroup aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract whole-number and same-denominator fraction parts once operands are compatible, including regrouping/borrowing across the whole when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
skills.merge_rationale: Merged because borrowing across the whole is not an independent phase; it is a contingent extension of aligned subtraction that occurs only when direct subtraction produces an insufficient fractional part. In the dossiers, S04 appears immediately after or within S03-based subtraction work, and both belong to the same execution stage.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the resulting fraction or mixed-number expression to lowest terms, or rewrite zero-fraction/whole-valued results in simplest form.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept as a single skill because simplification has distinct error patterns and remains diagnostically useful apart from computation and final formatting.

skills.name: Express final answer
skills.definition: Assemble computed whole and fractional parts into the final mixed number, fraction, or integer form.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept as a single skill because final assembly is a presentation/composition step that can succeed or fail independently of subtraction and simplification.

skills.name: Prepare operands for subtraction
skills.definition: Rewrite operands into a subtraction-ready form by normalizing whole or mixed numbers and, when needed, creating equivalent fractions with a common denominator.
skills.merge_rationale: Further merged from the K=5 level because both skills are preparatory transformations applied before core subtraction begins. In practice, they serve the same problem-solving phase: making operands structurally compatible. Although diagnostically distinguishable at finer grain, they can be combined meaningfully at a coarser level as setup.

skills.name: Subtract and regroup aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction on compatible whole and fraction parts, including borrowing/regrouping across the whole when necessary.
skills.merge_rationale: Retained from the K=5 level because subtraction and borrowing form a unified execution phase, with borrowing as a conditional subprocedure of subtraction rather than a separate broad competency.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or rewrite it in simplest whole-number form when appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification remains a common and instructionally important post-computation error point.

skills.name: Express final answer
skills.definition: Present the final value by combining whole and fractional parts into a mixed number, fraction, or integer.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final expression is a distinct output-formatting step and should not be conflated with simplification, which may or may not occur before it.

aggregation_notes: The main aggregation logic follows natural phases of fraction-subtraction problem solving: setup, execution, post-processing, and final expression. For K=5, the strongest merge is S03 with S04 because borrowing/regrouping is a conditional extension of aligned subtraction and does not usually stand alone in worked solutions. S01 and S02 were not merged at K=5 because common-denominator work and operand normalization produce different student errors and can occur independently. For K=4, S01 and S02 were merged into a broader preparation skill because both are pre-subtraction transformations that make operands compatible for computation. S05 and S06 were kept separate even at K=4 because simplifying a result and expressing the final answer are different cognitive operations with different error patterns; a student may compute and combine correctly yet fail to reduce, or simplify correctly yet mishandle final mixed-number expression.
